@RepBost You would vote to take access to healthcare away from millions of Americans in a heartbeat.

Critical Access Hospitals like Hamilton Memorial are lifelines for rural communities—when Washington’s bloated health bureaucracies siphon billions into administrative overhead instead of frontline care. HHS spending ballooned from $1.2 trillion in 2019 to $1.7 trillion by 2024, yet rural facilities still scramble for resources.

The real fix? Redirect every dollar wasted on redundant federal programs into these lean, local providers that actually deliver care. If 25-bed hospitals can stabilize patients faster than urban centers while operating on fractions of the budget, why does D.C. keep funding paper-pushers over practitioners?

Prioritize facilities proving efficiency works—not more bureaucratic “solutions.”

Honored to see AANA’s focus on veterans’ care, but let’s cut through the DC theatrics. CRNAs deliver quality anesthesia without the bureaucratic bloat of physician oversight—25 states already let them practice autonomously because it works. The real issue? Medicare’s outdated rules that waste taxpayer dollars forcing redundant supervision.

AANA-backed legislation to expand CRNA authority in VA facilities would save millions annually while speeding up surgery access for vets. Instead of fly-in photo ops, Congress should pass reforms that slash red tape and redirect savings to actual care—not administrative gatekeeping.

Efficiency isn’t optional when lives are on the line.
